findings.title: All 119 AGND F.Cu-to-In1 laser vias on each board use 0.25 mm pads on 0.15 mm holes, some sit close to the edge or to other holes, and PCBWay, the fabricator now chosen, has not confirmed them.
findings.what: Each board stitches the F.Cu AGND pour to In1 with 119 one-level blind vias. Each is drawn as a 0.15 mm hole in a 0.25 mm pad, which leaves a 0.05 mm copper ring. Blind vias are made by laser, and JLCPCB asks for a pad at least 0.15 mm larger than the hole, 0.30 mm here. Five of these vias also sit closer to the routed edge than JLCPCB's 0.35 mm. 18 hole pairs involving them are closer than its 0.24 mm spacing for different nets, and one same-net pair is closer than its 0.13 mm. The fix plan's step to resize them (A-0a) was not carried into V4. At PCBWay the 0.05 mm ring falls in the general high-difficulty tier already covered by AB-05.
findings.evidence: board_stats.txt shows 'Micro vias: 0' and 139/141 blind vias. vias.csv shows span 1-2 at 0.15/0.25 mm, 119 per board, all /AGND. Against JLCPCB: the 0.1 mm dielectric is inside 0.05-0.127 mm, the 0.15 mm hole is larger than the 0.1 mm dielectric, and the 0.9:1 depth ratio is within 1:1, so these pass. The 0.25 mm pad is under 0.30 mm and fails on 119/119. 111 of the 119 have room for a 0.30 mm pad (a review working file (not published)). 18 different-net hole pairs are under 0.24 mm, the closest 0.176 mm (via_rules.py). Resizing to 0.10/0.25 mm (0.075 mm ring) needs no extra room and leaves 4 edge vias and 12 close pairs. It sits exactly at JLCPCB's 1:1 dielectric limit, which FAQ 5 allows but the table's row G does not.
findings.source: JLCPCB 'HDI PCB Capabilities & FAQ' (last updated 9 Nov 2026), FAQ 5, 8 and 9. Its rules: blind-via pad ≥ hole + 0.15 mm, dielectric 0.05-0.127 mm, hole larger than dielectric, depth:diameter ≤ 1:1, blind via to routed edge ≥ 0.35 mm, hole edges ≥ 0.24 mm apart for different nets and ≥ 0.13 mm for the same net. https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/hdi-pcb-capabilities-faq (values re-read on the page by the merge re-check). findings.what: Each die has 176 fingers 0.1016 mm wide at 0.2032 mm pitch; the side fingers are 0.254 mm long. Würth's rules ask for at least 0.150 mm width (and draw 0.300 mm length), and the EPFL bonder guideline asks for 0.300 x 0.500 mm board pads. On each side most outer-column fingers sit behind an inner-column finger of another net. Their wires must clear the inner finger's stitch from above, so two loop heights are needed. Corner and top-row end wires run about 42-65° off the finger axis. The June board, with the same per-die geometry, was bonded, so this works with the designer's bonding house. What is new on V4 is the middle: die 1's right outer row and die 2's left outer row merge into 33 shared fingers (0.378 x 0.1016 mm). Each needs one stitch from each die, from opposite sides.

findings.title: The opened finger rows leave bare ±8 V stimulation copper 0.08-0.10 mm apart, so an encapsulant is required, but the rows end 0.41-0.50 mm from three routed edges, which leaves no room for a dam to hold it.
findings.what: V4 opens the mask over each finger row as one block. Inside the rows the VDD10 and VSS10 fingers are 0.102 mm apart, and a VSS10 track enters the middle opening 0.082 mm from a VDD10 finger. That is bare plated copper with about 20 V across it, on a head-worn board, so protection has to come from an encapsulant over dies, wires and rows. A dispensed dam (a bead of stiff epoxy that stops the flow and sets the height) needs about 0.65-0.8 mm of board outside the outermost bonds. Here the opened rows end 0.41-0.50 mm from the left, right and probe edges; only the J4 side has room (2.30 mm to J4's pads). So the encapsulant must be held by a fixture or by the board edges, and its height over the dies is set only by volume and flow.
findings.where: Both V4 boards, F.Cu/F.Mask. VDD10/VSS10 fingers P10/M10 at x 124.98, 135.25, 135.37 and 145.63 (y 76.68/76.48). VSS10 track from (134.87, 76.51) to (135.21, 76.51). The left outer opening starts at x 124.805 (edge 124.339), the right ends at x 145.809 (edge 146.307), and the side openings run to y 84.065 (probe edge 84.472). The top-row opening starts at y 74.993; J4's pads end at y 72.69. The area to cover is about 21 x 9.5 mm.
findings.evidence: In this pass, from the V4 dumps: the VSS10 track is 0.082 mm from U01_BCD1 P10_R and 0.086 mm from U01_BCD2 P10_L; M10/P10 fingers are 0.1016 mm apart; there are 11 F.Mask row rectangles. Opening to edge: 0.466 mm (left), 0.498 mm (right), 0.408 mm (probe). Top opening to J4 pads: 2.30 mm. No dam ring, keep-out or encapsulation outline exists on any layer. The height limit over the dies is in AB-06.

findings.title: None of the 30 capacitors on either board has a capacitance value, voltage rating or part number, including four 0201 parts on the ±10 V rails.
findings.what: Every capacitor is the bare symbol 'C_Small_US' with an 0201 footprint and empty value, rating and part-number fields. findings.title: Nothing in the V4 package tells the bonding house where, which way or how to bond the dies: there is no die outline, centre, orientation mark or V4 bond diagram, and no wire, attach or encapsulation specification.
findings.what: V4 correctly marks U01_BCD1/BCD2 not placed and leaves them out of the BOM and position files, but nothing replaces that data for the bonding house. Each U01 footprint has only its 176 fingers and 5-6 mask openings, and neither board nor schematic carries a note or title block. The only bond map is the designer's photo of the bonded June board (slide 2). It matches 170 of the 176 V4 fingers wire for wire, but it names no pads. It also does not show what is new on V4: two dies sharing 33 middle fingers, and seven changed fingers per die (CGEN_BK removed, DISC_OUT and RRST_DIGITAL moved to the inner row, four small moves). The die centre is not the footprint origin. The June die sat about 0.24-0.25 mm left of and 0.25-0.27 mm below it, and a die placed on the origin would reach 0.01 mm into the right inner fingers.
findings.where: Both V4 boards: U01_BCD1 at (130.369, 80.205) and U01_BCD2 at (140.755, 80.205), footprint chip:U01_BCD_OFF_CHIP, DNP, no BOM, no position file. Their only graphics are F.Mask shapes (6 and 5). Estimated die centres are near (130.12-130.13, 80.45-80.48) and (140.51-140.52, 80.45-80.48).
findings.evidence: In this pass, from the V4 dumps: U01 dnp, no_bom and no_pos are all True; the only graphics are 6/5 F.Mask shapes, with no F.Fab, silkscreen or courtyard; title blocks are empty. Photo analysis (a review working file (not published)): 179 gold balls = 177 June fingers plus second stitches on LDGND_11/RDGND_11. The die pad ring and the June finger ring match in number, order and corner layout. 170/176 V4 fingers lie within 0.002 mm of their June positions relative to the ring. On the June frame the die spans x 126.21-134.43, y 77.12-84.16 (image5) or x 126.28-134.35, y 77.15-84.07 (image4). Placed on the V4 origin, its right edge would be at x 134.419, past the inner finger edge at 134.408. CGEN_BK, DISC_OUT and RRST_DIGITAL all carried wires in June. At their June positions on V4 they would overlap die 2's VCM, AGND2 and CLKH fingers, which is why they moved. The V4 question list asks the bonding house only about finish, die-attach pad, back-side parts and mask openings.

findings.title: Each stack's 44 chip outputs return through only two DGND contacts at each 80-pin joint; the ASIC designer confirmed two separate grounds joined at one point on the FPGA-LDO board and a final pin order, so only a bring-up check remains.
findings.what: Each 80-pin joint has AGND only on pins 42/44 and DGND only on 46/48. In a stack, the return current of four chips' 44 outputs flows through those two DGND contacts at the FPGA-LDO joint, and the far board's 22 outputs cross a second joint with the same returns. A signal that changes layer between F.Cu (over AGND on In1) and B.Cu (over DGND on In8) needs its return current to jump between the two grounds. No capacitor or tie joins AGND and DGND on either board, so that return goes through the connector or the dies. R2S-05 proposed tying the spare pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 to ground, but in V4 and pin map V6 those pins carry top-chip outputs.
findings.where: Both V4 boards: J3/J4 pins 42/44 (/AGND) and 46/48 (/DGND). FPGA-LDO A and router: 42/44 AGND, 46/48 GND; AGND meets GND at NT1 (Option A) or behind J5 (Option B). Pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 are T_READ(2), T_D<8>(2), T_D<7>(2), T_D<6>(2), T_D<2>(2) and T_D<6>.
findings.evidence: In this pass: ground-pin and spare-pin nets read from both V4 boards. No capacitor has both /AGND and /DGND pads (the rails go to AGND, DVDD to DGND). FPGA-LDO A/router pins 46/48 are GND (exports/ldo_a and exports/ldo_b_router connectors.csv). R2S-05's order-of-magnitude estimate assumes 1.5 ns edges, about 12 pF per line and 0.4 nH for two contacts. On that basis 32 data lines switching together draw about 0.38 A and bounce each joint about 0.1 V, so the far chips sit about 0.2 V off the FPGA's ground. pair-power F5: 53 (bottom) / 31 (top) connector signal nets change between F.Cu and B.Cu. The fix-plan critic notes that the DGND-on-spare items conflict with V6.

findings.title: Each die sits on closed solder mask over 12 capped rail vias (two each of the 1.5 V VDD_FE, VDD_ADC, VDD_DRIVER, DVDD and REF_VDD and the 0.75 V REF_VCM), each 0.077 mm from AGND copper, so no die-attach pad can be opened, and nothing tells the bonder to use a non-conductive attach.
findings.what: With the die placed as the designer's slides show (8.1 x 7.0 mm), the mask stays closed under both dies, so each die's back rests on mask. DGND vias and 5-8 control lines also run there. The V4 question list still offers the bonding house a 'die-attach pad'. If the mask were opened for one, a conductive attach would join all of these to each other and to the die substrate, whose potential is not recorded. The June die sat only over ground copper plus one CHIP_RESET via and one CLKH via, so its attach process does not prove V4 safe.
findings.where: Both boards, F.Cu/F.Mask under U01_BCD1 (x 126.066-134.166) and U01_BCD2 (x 136.452-144.552), with the die bottom at y 84.0 (or flush at 84.472). Capped rail vias at BCD1 x 129.55-133.45 and BCD2 x 137.25-141.00, y 79.05-83.95.

findings.title: No flatness limit is set for the ASIC boards, although Hirose allows only 0.02 mm of bow across each DF40 and a standard order allows about 0.09-0.13 mm.
findings.what: Hirose asks that the board bow no more than 0.02 mm at the middle of a DF40, measured against the connector's two ends. A normal fab order guarantees bow and twist only as a share of length: 0.75 % in PCBWay's normal class (and in IPC) and 0.5 % in its hardest class. Over the 17.5 mm connector that is about 0.13 mm and 0.09 mm. Each ASIC board carries a DF40 on both faces at the same spot, its top copper is about 53 % filled against 15-17 % on the bottom, and a 0.8 mm board would be eight times less stiff than 1.6 mm. No record or order text sets a flatness limit.
findings.where: Both boards: J4 DF40C-80DP on F.Cu at (135.54, 71.005) and J3 DF40C-80DS on B.Cu at (135.54, 71.01). The connector bodies are 17.52 mm and 18.6 mm long.
findings.evidence: Hirose catalog p21: board warpage at most 0.02 mm at the centre, relative to both ends of the connector. Hirose drawings: header length 17.52 mm (EDC3-311351-00), receptacle 18.6 mm (EDC3-311352-00), lead coplanarity 0.1 mm. 0.02 / 17.52 = 0.11 %. PCBWay Advanced item 35: bow and twist ≤ 0.75 % normal, < 0.5 % high. JLCPCB gives no value. Copper after refill (a review working file (not published)): top board F.Cu 53.3 %, inner layers 79-89 %, B.Cu 15.1 % (17.4 % on the bottom board). In this pass, board_stats.txt gives front copper 237.0 mm² against back 66.9 mm² (top board) and 79.0 mm² (bottom board). SYS-48 quotes the same Hirose line but acts only on the reflow count, and the LDOB-20 flatness note covers only Option B.

findings.title: The 8.1 x 7.0 mm die fits the 8.583 mm finger opening with only about 0.24 mm per side and 0.19 mm to the V4 row openings. The June board proves the fit with the designer's die and bonder, but V4 records neither die thickness nor bond recipe.
findings.what: The designer's slide 1 draws the die 8.1 mm wide along its 46-pad row and 7 mm tall, and slide 2 shows that row bonded to the top finger row, so on V4 the die's 8.1 mm side runs along x. In this pass, the 11 via positions and spans were confirmed on both V4 boards.

JLCPCB PCB Capabilities (inner-layer via hole to copper 0.2 mm), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities. PCBWay PCB Capabilities, Advanced item 13 (hole to copper on 10+ layers: ≥ 10 mil normal, 7-8 mil high), https://www.pcbway.com/capabilities.html.
